target_ref_note: Pinned to OWASP crAPI v1.1.6 (released 2025-09-30), Apache-2.0. 'completely ridiculous API' — a deliberately vulnerable microservices app: services/identity (Java 17 / Spring Boot), services/workshop (Python / Django REST), services/community (Go / gqlgen GraphQL), services/web (TypeScript / React), plus Docker-Compose + k8s deploy/. Chosen as the third E2E target because one repo covers THREE categories Juice Shop cannot: token_scope (JWT/JWK issues), deployment (intentionally weak compose/k8s posture), and partial mitm (inter-service HTTP calls). Microservice file paths are version-sensitive — re-verify the service/<svc>/.../*.{java,py,go} layout if you re-pin. Select with: scripts/run-e2e-test.sh --target crapi.
notes: Match rule identical to expected-findings.json (see tests/e2e/assertions.py). Several fixtures here are SOFT (must_match:false): crAPI's flaws are runtime-behavioural (BOLA via path param, mass assignment via extra JSON keys) and a static auditor may surface the class without pinning the exact handler. The hard fixtures are the ones a competent static pass over the source must reach: hard-coded JWT secret/JWK, the SSRF, and the deployment misconfig.

schema_changelog.v3: see expected-findings.json — negative_expectations[] decoys + precision/recall scorer.

expectations.description: BOLA / IDOR — vehicle-location endpoint returns another user's vehicle by vehicleId path param with no ownership check.
expectations.rationale: Classic crAPI BOLA: GET /identity/api/v2/vehicle/{vehicleId}/location resolves the vehicle without checking it belongs to the authenticated user. CWE-639 authorization-bypass-via-key; alternate CWEs cover broader access-control taxonomies.

expectations.description: BOLA on the mechanic/report flow — reading another user's service report by id.
expectations.rationale: Soft: the Django workshop service exposes mechanic service-report reads keyed by id without scoping to the requester. Requires per-view authz tracing (cat-02 IDOR fan-out).

expectations.description: Hard-coded / weak JWT signing key (or JWK with a predictable/embedded private key) used to sign and verify access tokens.
expectations.rationale: crAPI ships a JWT/JWK token-scope weakness (key confusion / embedded key / unverified kid). CWE-321 hard-coded crypto key, CWE-347 improper signature verification, CWE-522 insufficiently-protected credentials all in scope. This is the token_scope ground truth Juice Shop lacks.

expectations.description: JWT signature verification weakness — algorithm not pinned / alg confusion / unverified token allowed.
expectations.rationale: Soft: crAPI's token validation accepts tokens signed in ways it should reject (the canonical 'forge a token with the leaked/embedded key' lab). Single-shot auditors may fold this into crapi-03 rather than enumerate the verification flaw separately.

expectations.description: Mass assignment — request body binds directly to a model, letting a client set protected fields (e.g. credit/balance, role, isAdmin) it should not control.
expectations.rationale: crAPI's coupon/mechanic flows accept extra JSON keys that overwrite server-controlled fields (DRF serializer with fields='__all__' or a Spring DTO with no field allow-list). CWE-915 mass-assignment is the precise tag.

expectations.description: SSRF — server fetches an attacker-controlled URL (e.g. the 'check coupon' / merchant callback that the server-side requests outbound).
expectations.rationale: crAPI's server makes an outbound HTTP request to a client-supplied URL (the merchant/coupon validation callback), the canonical API SSRF. CWE-918. alternate category mitm reflects that the same outbound call is also an unauthenticated inter-service hop.

expectations.description: Deployment misconfiguration — Docker-Compose / k8s manifests run services with weak posture (hard-coded secrets in env, debug enabled, privileged/host networking, or no resource/security context).
expectations.rationale: crAPI's compose/k8s setup is intentionally weak (secrets in env, Django DEBUG, no securityContext). This is the deployment-category ground truth Juice Shop's hardened distroless image cannot provide. CWE-1188 insecure-default-init; alternates cover hard-coded secrets / perms.

negative_expectations.description: Spring Security password storage uses BCryptPasswordEncoder — correct password hashing, not a weak-crypto finding.
negative_expectations.rationale: crAPI's identity service configures a BCryptPasswordEncoder bean. bcrypt is the recommended algorithm; flagging the password-encoder config as weak hashing is a false positive. (The real crypto/token weakness is the JWT key, crapi-03 — a different file and class.)

negative_expectations.description: Django ORM querysets (Model.objects.filter / get) parameterize SQL — using the ORM is NOT SQL injection.
negative_expectations.rationale: The workshop service queries via the Django ORM, which parameterizes. A finding tagging models.py as CWE-89 is the classic ORM false positive — there is no raw-SQL .raw()/.extra() with interpolation in the model layer.

negative_expectations.description: Parameterized prepared statement / repository finder in the identity service is not SQLi.
negative_expectations.rationale: Spring Data JPA repositories use bound parameters; flagging a derived-query repository method as SQL injection is an FP. crAPI's injectable surface is its authz (BOLA) and SSRF, not raw SQL in the repository layer.

gated_categories.llm: crAPI has no LLM SDK; cat-09 gated off. Absent phase-05-llm-*.jsonl is pass-via-skip.
gated_categories.agentic: crAPI exposes APIs but no MCP server / agent-tool-definition surface; profile.mcp_agentic.detected=false → cat-agentic gated off. Absent phase-05-agentic-*.jsonl is a LEGITIMATE skip — do NOT demand agentic findings here.

always_on_categories.supply_chain: Always-on. crAPI has pom.xml (Java), requirements.txt (Python), go.mod (Go), package.json (TS) — a rich multi-ecosystem dependency surface; cat-supply_chain is expected to execute across all four. No specific supply_chain fixture is pinned (CVEs drift).
